To find the quadratic polynomial \( p(x) = ax^2 + bx + c \) that satisfies the conditions \( p(-2) = 13 \), \( p(1) = -2 \), and \( p(3) = 8 \), we can set up a system of equations based on these conditions.

First, substitute \( x = -2 \) into the polynomial:
\[
p(-2) = a(-2)^2 + b(-2) + c = 4a - 2b + c = 13
\]
This gives us the first equation:
\[
4a - 2b + c = 13 \quad \text{(1)}
\]

Next, substitute \( x = 1 \) into the polynomial:
\[
p(1) = a(1)^2 + b(1) + c = a + b + c = -2
\]
This gives us the second equation:
\[
a + b + c = -2 \quad \text{(2)}
\]

Finally, substitute \( x = 3 \) into the polynomial:
\[
p(3) = a(3)^2 + b(3) + c = 9a + 3b + c = 8
\]
This gives us the third equation:
\[
9a + 3b + c = 8 \quad \text{(3)}
\]

We now have a system of three linear equations:
\[
\begin{cases}
4a - 2b + c = 13 \\
a + b + c = -2 \\
9a + 3b + c = 8
\end{cases}
\]

To eliminate \( c \), subtract equation (2) from equation (1):
\[
(4a - 2b + c) - (a + b + c) = 13 - (-2)
\]
\[
4a - 2b + c - a - b - c = 13 + 2
\]
\[
3a - 3b = 15
\]
\[
a - b = 5 \quad \text{(4)}
\]

Next, subtract equation (2) from equation (3):
\[
(9a + 3b + c) - (a + b + c) = 8 - (-2)
\]
\[
9a + 3b + c - a - b - c = 8 + 2
\]
\[
8a + 2b = 10
\]
\[
4a + b = 5 \quad \text{(5)}
\]

Now we have a new system of two equations:
\[
\begin{cases}
a - b = 5 \\
4a + b = 5
\end{cases}
\]

Add these two equations to eliminate \( b \):
\[
(a - b) + (4a + b) = 5 + 5
\]
\[
5a = 10
\]
\[
a = 2
\]

Substitute \( a = 2 \) back into equation (4):
\[
2 - b = 5
\]
\[
-b = 3
\]
\[
b = -3
\]

Finally, substitute \( a = 2 \) and \( b = -3 \) back into equation (2):
\[
2 + (-3) + c = -2
\]
\[
-1 + c = -2
\]
\[
c = -1
\]

\[
p(x) = 2x^2 - 3x - 1
\]

\[
\boxed{2x^2 - 3x - 1}
